json.title: Compact the log in the background
json.body:
The log grows without bound until `compact()` is called by hand, and calling it on the main thread stalls a frame on large stores (about 40 ms at 50k entries on my phone).

This moves compaction to an idle callback:

- `Store` schedules `compactSoon()` after every 500 appends or when the log passes 2 MB
- compaction runs in slices of 200 entries and yields between slices
- a write during a slice is appended to a side log and replayed when the slice ends

### Numbers

| entries | before | after (longest slice) |
|---|---|---|
| 10k | 9 ms | 1.1 ms |
| 50k | 41 ms | 1.3 ms |
| 200k | 170 ms | 1.4 ms |

Closes #190.

@juniper-vale could you look at the side log? I am not sure the replay order is right when a slice is cancelled.
Nice numbers. Does this change anything for people who call `compact()` themselves today?
No: `compact()` still runs everything at once and returns when it is done. The background path is only for the automatic case.

Bundle size: **+0.6 kB** (gzip), 14.2 kB total.

Coverage: 91.4% (+0.3%).
Ran it against the relay soak test for an hour, no stalls and memory flat.

json.title: Let a store say which fields merge as sets
json.body:
Today every field merges last-writer-wins. That is wrong for tags and members: two devices that each add a tag offline should end up with both.

```ts
const notes = tidepool.store("notes", {
  merge: { tags: "set", title: "lww" },
});
```

A `"set"` field keeps adds and removes as separate entries (an observed-remove set), so a remove only wins over the adds it has seen.

- [x] `set` merge for arrays of strings
- [x] wire format: a set field travels as its add and remove entries
- [ ] migration for stores that already hold tags as plain arrays
- [ ] docs
Love this. One question: what does a reader of an old client see when it receives a set field it does not know about?
An old client sees the field as an object and ignores it today. I will add a version byte so the relay can refuse to forward it to clients older than 0.9.
Drive-by from pebble-kv land: we store OR-set tombstones with the observed dots compressed as ranges, which kept them about 8x smaller. Happy to share notes.
@teo-lindqvist yes please! Tombstone size is the part I was worried about.
Tested on the fern playground's shared snippets: two tabs offline, each tags a snippet, both tags survive. :tada:

json.title: Merge loses a delete when two devices edit offline
json.body:
**What happened**

Device A deletes a note while offline. Device B, also offline, edits the same note's title. When both come back, the note is back with B's title and A's delete is gone.

**Expected**

I am not sure. Either the delete wins, or the edit wins and the app is told about the conflict. Silently resurrecting the note surprised our users.

**Steps**

1. Two clients on the same store, both offline
2. A: `notes.delete("n1")`
3. B: `notes.update("n1", { title: "Groceries" })`
4. Bring both online and sync

tidepool 0.8.2, relay 0.8.2, Chrome 140 and Safari 19.
Reproduced. The delete is a tombstone with time 100, B's edit has time 104, and last-writer-wins on the whole record lets the newer edit win.
That matches what we see. Is there a way to make deletes win today?
Not today. I think we want a per-store choice: `onConflict: "delete-wins" | "edit-wins" | (a, b) => ...`. @juniper-vale this touches your set-merge work, what do you think?
Agreed on a per-store rule. I would make delete-wins the default for new stores and keep edit-wins for existing ones so nothing changes under people. I can take it after #214.
Added the `needs repro` label off by mistake, sorry. Removed it.

json.title: Relay drops a client that sleeps longer than the ping interval
json.body:
A phone that sleeps for more than 30 s misses two pings and the relay closes its socket. On wake, the client reconnects and sends its whole log again instead of resuming.

The relay should keep a closed peer's cursor for a few minutes so the client can resume.
I will take this one. Plan: keep a cursor per peer id for 10 minutes after the socket closes; a reconnect with the same id resumes from it.
Sounds good. Our battery tests would love this: a full resend costs us about 2 MB per wake on a big store.

routes.text:
# tidepool

Offline-first sync for small apps. Every change is an entry in a local log;
devices exchange their logs through a tiny relay and merge them the same way,
so two phones that edited offline agree once they meet.

- **Small**: 14 kB gzipped, no dependencies
- **Local first**: reads and writes never wait for the network
- **Any transport**: the relay is optional; peers can sync over any byte pipe

## Install

```sh
npm install @driftwood/tidepool
```

## Use

```ts
import { tidepool } from "@driftwood/tidepool";

const db = await tidepool.open("groceries");
const items = db.store("items");

await items.put("milk", { done: false, qty: 2 });
items.watch((change) => render(change));

db.sync("wss://relay.example/sync");
```

## How it works

1. A write appends an entry (key, value, time, device) to the log
2. The log is compacted in the background to the newest entry per key
3. Syncing sends the entries a peer has not seen, by vector clock
4. Merging picks a winner per field: last writer wins, or a set

See [docs/storage.md](docs/storage.md) and [docs/protocol.md](docs/protocol.md).

## Running the relay

```sh
npx @driftwood/tidepool-relay --port 8787 --data ./relay-data
```

The relay keeps no application data, only the entries peers have not yet
picked up, for up to 30 days.

## Status

| Feature | State |
|---|---|
| Last-writer-wins fields | stable |
| Set fields | in review (#214) |
| Background compaction | in review (#217) |
| End-to-end encryption | planned |

## License

MIT

# Changelog

## 0.9.0

- Peers resume from a cursor after a reconnect instead of resending
- `store.watch()` hands over the change and the previous value
- The relay drops entries older than 30 days

## 0.8.2

- Fix: a store opened twice in one tab shared a cursor
- Docs: running the relay on a Raspberry Pi

## 0.8.1

- Fix: tombstones were sent to peers that had already seen them

## 0.8.0

- Vector clocks replace per-device counters
- Wire format 3

export const encode = (value: unknown) => new TextEncoder().encode(JSON.stringify(value));
export const decode = <T>(bytes: Uint8Array) => JSON.parse(new TextDecoder().decode(bytes)) as T;

# Storage

Every write is an entry at the end of the log:
key, value, time and the device that wrote it.

## Compaction

Call `store.compact()` to keep only the newest entry for each key.

## Limits

A store holds up to 2 MB of log before it asks to be compacted.
IndexedDB keeps the log between sessions; in Node it is a file per store.

# Protocol

Peers exchange entries over a websocket. Each message is one entry:
a version byte (3), then the entry as JSON.

1. On connect, a peer sends its vector clock
2. The relay answers with every entry the clock has not seen
3. From then on, each new entry is forwarded as it arrives

A peer that reconnects with the same id resumes from its cursor.

routes.text:
# trailmap

Draw a GPX track and its elevation in your terminal.

```
$ trailmap examples/ridge-loop.gpx
  ridge loop   14.2 km   +612 m   2:41
  .....*****.......
  ...**.....**.....
  ..*.........*....
  ...**......*.....
  .....******......
```

## Install

```sh
cargo install trailmap
```

## Options

- `--width`, `--height`: the plot's size in cells
- `--no-map`: only the elevation plot
- `--units imperial`: miles and feet

## Why

I wanted to glance at a run from an SSH session without opening a browser.

name = "lsm-notes"
version = "0.1.0"

# Memtables

Writes land in a sorted in-memory table first. When it passes a size, it is frozen and a new one takes writes.

# Flushing

A frozen memtable is written out as one sorted run: a file of blocks and an index.

# Compaction

Leveled compaction keeps reads cheap; tiered keeps writes cheap. Most stores pick a mix.

json.name: 0.9.0: resume after reconnect
json.body:
## What changed

- Peers resume from a cursor after a reconnect instead of resending their whole log (#209)
- `store.watch()` hands over the change and the previous value
- The relay drops entries older than 30 days

## Upgrading

The relay and clients can be upgraded in any order. A 0.8 client talking to a 0.9 relay resends as before.

**Full changelog**: v0.8.2...v0.9.0

- Fix: a store opened twice in one tab shared a cursor
- Docs: running the relay on a Raspberry Pi
- Fix: tombstones were sent to peers that had already seen them

json.name: 0.8.0: vector clocks
json.body:
## Breaking

Wire format 3. Upgrade the relay first.

## What changed

- Vector clocks replace per-device counters, so three or more devices merge correctly
- Smaller sync messages: about 40% fewer bytes on a typical store

Resize every photo in a folder to 1600 px, keeping EXIF dates

shrink.sh.content:
#!/bin/sh
# shrink.sh <folder>: every JPEG to 1600 px on its long side
set -e
for f in "$1"/*.jpg; do
  magick "$f" -resize '1600x1600>' -quality 85 "${f%.jpg}-small.jpg"
  exiftool -q -overwrite_original -TagsFromFile "$f" -DateTimeOriginal "${f%.jpg}-small.jpg"
done
